items.summary: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

items.headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

items.headline: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

items.headline: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.

items.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains optimistic Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.
items.summary: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

items.headline: Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

items.headline: The Rams signed Scott to the practice squad Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: With Jordan Whittington (back), Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, the Rams are looking to bolster depth within the receiving corps. While Scott is on the practice squad at the moment, there's a chance he could get on the field for at least one regular-season contest. The 25-year-old appeared in a combined 28 regular-season games for the Bears in 2023 and 2024, totaling 18 catches (33 targets) for 173 yards.

items.headline: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

items.headline: Bell (knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Colts.
items.summary: The rookie sat out both Thursday and Friday's practices before being given a doubtful designation for Sunday's contest, and his inactive status is now official. With Bell, who'd posted a 7-56-0 line on 10 targets in Weeks 7 and 8 before being blanked against the Lions in Week 9, sitting out Sunday, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert could share No. 3 receiver snaps while working with new starting quarterback Kyle McCord.

items.headline: Coleman wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for 16 yards.
items.summary: Coleman logged just 11 offensive snaps, and he's settled back in as the Dolphins' fourth receiver with all three of Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell healthy ahead of him on the depth chart. Coleman, a fifth-round rookie out of Missouri has no fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Cook reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Cook was elevated to serve as the team's primary backup quarterback behind Kyle McCord during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, but he did not play in the game. Cook will likely be elevated again prior to the team's Week 11 matchup with the Bills.

items.headline: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

items.headline: Reagor reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Reagor played eight offensive snaps and was unable to haul in his sole target during Sunday's loss to the Colts. The wide receiver also logged one special-teams snap in the contest.

items.headline: Traore went without a target while playing six of the Dolphins' 69 snaps on offense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: Meanwhile, Traore tied a season-high with 23 snaps on special teams, where he continues to receive the bulk of his playing time. The reserve tight end has played in all nine of the Dolphins' games to date but has gone without a reception while being targeted once across 39 total snaps on offense.

items.headline: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Wayne popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quadriceps injury, which prevented him from suiting up for Friday's session. He won't be available for Sunday's contest, and it appears the Dolphins will also be without rookie third-rounder Chris Bell (knee), who is listed as doubtful. Wayne's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Brosmer was the Vikings' backup for Week 9 against the Bills and ended up seeing the field late in the fourth quarter, when he completed six of seven pass attempts for 58 yards. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and he will serve as Minnesota's starter Sunday while Carson Wentz operates as the backup. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) sidelined, that leaves Brosmer as the emergency QB3, which prohibits the latter from playing unless both Cousins and Wentz leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Culp reverted to the Vikings' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Culp will return to the practice squad after he was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end didn't record any stats while playing 13 snaps on special teams, and he could be elevated again in Week 11 if T.J. Hockenson (wrist) remains sidelined against the 49ers.

items.headline: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

items.headline: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

items.headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Hockenson was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but it sounds like the tight end has a chance to return to practice after logging DNPs last week. In Hockenson's absence versus Green Bay in Week 10, fellow TE Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and a TD.

items.headline: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
items.summary: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Claiborne (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Bankston to the practice squad Wednesday, Rob Kleifield of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Bankston was cut from the Packers' practice squad Oct. 20, but the New Mexico product will find a new home with the Vikings and stay in the NFC North division. He was with Minnesota during the tail end of the 2025 season and was with the Giants in training camp before being cut by New York on Aug. 29. Bankston's addition gives the Vikings additional backfield depth and a potential contributor on special teams.

items.headline: Beckham signed with the Vikings' practice squad Thursday
items.summary: Beckham rejoins the Vikings after being released by the team earlier in the week. The veteran was active for Monday Night Football in Week 9 but played only two snaps. He'll remain in the system and could be called up to the active roster if and when the Vikings need more depth at receiver.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Lauter to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding moves, the Saints also signed tight end Treyton Welch to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Lauter started with the Raiders as an undrafted free agent during the offseason and is still waiting to make his regular-season NFL debut.

items.headline: Brown (hamstring) was spotted walking around with a limp in the locker room following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
items.summary: Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

items.headline: Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

items.headline: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
items.summary: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
items.summary: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

items.headline: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

items.headline: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
items.summary: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

items.headline: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams.
items.summary: Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but available as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: As he has for the first nine games of his career, Morton only will see the field if both starter Drake Maye and backup Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
items.summary: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of snaps, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. He's also been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. Raridon is averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

items.headline: Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Arkin to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The tight end was cut from the 53-man roster Monday and cleared waivers. The undrafted rookie has appeared in five games for New England this season but hasn't been targeted on 60 offensive snaps. Arkin has played another 41 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
items.summary: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

items.headline: Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: Donaldson will miss a third straight game, while Travis Etienne (hamstring) has a chance to return from injured reserve. With Etienne listed as questionable, Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara could have significant roles. Donaldson mostly has played in obvious passing situations this year, often staying in as a blocker.

items.headline: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.headline: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

items.headline: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
items.summary: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

items.headline: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

items.headline: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

items.headline: White reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With Travis Etienne (IR, hamstring) still sidelined and Kendre Miller cut over the weekend, White was elevated as the RB3 behind Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime. White played four offensive snaps against Cleveland on Sunday and rushed one time for five yards.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Wilson is the No. 3 quarterback behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. The inactive third option will only enter Sunday's game if Shough and Rattler must leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Welch to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding transactions, the Saints also signed tight end Matt Lauter to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Welch has already suited up for five games with New Orleans this season, with most of his snaps coming on special teams.

items.headline: Desrosiers carried the ball three times for 20 yards during the Giants' win over the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Desrosiers made his regular-season debut during the victory, serving as the team's No. 2 running back behind Devin Singletary, as Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury. With Skattebo now healthy again, Desrosiers will likely be relegated to a depth role during Thursday's matchup versus the Commanders.

items.headline: Fidone (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's contest in Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Fidone suited up for each of New York's previous three games before a Week 8 bye, but he's a healthy scratch against the Eagles. The second-year tight end has worked mostly on special teams this season and has one catch for 29 yards on one target over three contests. Fidone figures to be at risk for inactive status when the three tight ends ahead of him in the pecking order -- Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz -- are healthy.

items.headline: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
items.summary: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
items.summary: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlies Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over in that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.

items.headline: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

items.headline: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
items.summary: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
items.summary: Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Mafah reverted to the Giants' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With both Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Tyrone Tracy (IR, hamstring) sidelined, Mafah joined Greg Desrosiers as the healthy running backs behind Devin Singletary. Mafah played just 10 snaps on special teams and none on offense Sunday against Philly.

items.headline: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
items.summary: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

items.headline: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
items.summary: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

items.headline: The Giants signed Haener to their practice squad Saturday,Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Haener has been part of New York's active roster twice this season, and he was most recently waived by the team Thursday. The Fresno State product will remain in the organization on the practice squad, as the Giants have J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston as their quarterbacks on game days. Should one of those two get injured and need to miss time, Haener figures to be elevated or signed to the roster again.

items.headline: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis can be ignored in fantasy football moving forward. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests. Davis returned three kicks for 74 yards against Buffalo.

items.headline: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.headline: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor typically has handled larger snap shares.

items.headline: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
items.summary: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

items.headline: Patrick (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bills.
items.summary: Garrett Wilson (concussion), Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) have all been cleared to play Sunday, so Patrick will observe from the sidelines. Patrick hasn't played since Week 7 against the Dolphins, and his next opportunity to suit up is Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.headline: The Jets signed Manjack to the practice squad Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie receiver out of TCU had previously spent time with Denver in the offseason, appearing in all three preseason games while catching three of four targets for 40 yards. After failing to make the Broncos' roster heading into Week 1, Manjack had been a free agent before landing an opportunity with the Jets.

items.headline: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

items.headline: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

items.headline: Covey (knee) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Giants.
items.summary: Covey was again unable to practice during the week because of the knee injury he suffered back in Week 7 versus the Cowboys, and he'll miss his second straight game in Week 9. In his absence, 2025 fifth-rounder Jaydon Blue and 2024 second-rounder Cooper DeJean will likely continue to see increased opportunities in the return game.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
items.summary: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

items.headline: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

items.headline: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
items.summary: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

items.headline: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

items.headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: The Eagles released Pierce (undisclosed) from IR with an injury settlement Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.summary: Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another organization.

items.headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: Smith thus will sit out for the fifth time in six games due to a hamstring injury. Fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also won't play Sunday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to man the Eagles' receiving corps. Smith's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 22, versus the Steelers.

items.headline: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

items.headline: Wicks (ankle) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: After sitting out practice Friday, Wicks will miss a third straight game for Philadelphia. He'll now have the team's Week 10 bye to try and get right coming out of the break. The Eagles will continue to roll with Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper as their Nos. 1 and 2 receivers against New York this week.

items.headline: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday.
items.summary: Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but he now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If Shipley is able to suit up this weekend, he'll reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

items.headline: Blue was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Blue was let go by the Eagles after suiting up for the team in Weeks 8 and 9, a span in which he didn't record a carry and caught his only target for nine yards. Now that he's back on the team's practice squad, the 2025 fifth-rounder will give Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley-led RB corps an added depth option ahead of Week 11 action.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Rucci to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Rucci last spent time with the Chargers before being let go by the team ahead of Week 10. In six games with the Bolts, the 27-year-old recorded one reception for seven yards and a touchdown. The second-year pro will act as organizational depth after Zach Ertz was elevated to the active roster.

items.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

items.headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
items.summary: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

items.headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.
items.summary: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

items.headline: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.summary: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

items.headline: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
items.summary: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

items.headline: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

items.headline: Coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are "hopeful" they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.summary: The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

items.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.summary: Now that he's spent the required four games on IR while recovering from a finger injury, Wilson is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened this week. McCarthy expressed similar optimism that fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) will be able to come off IR this week, a development that could result in Wilson settling for a lesser role if both receivers are activated ahead of Sunday's contest. Despite a rough start to the season, Pittman signed a two-year, $35 million extension in March that likely affords him some security as a starter alongside DK Metcalf upon his return, which would leave Wilson to fend with rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart.

items.headline: Cooks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.summary: Mike Evans (Achilles) is also inactive for a third consecutive game, but Cooks' services are not needed Sunday due to the return of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the acquisition of Keenan Allen from the Colts on Tuesday. It's unclear if Cooks will have any role in the 49ers' offense once Evans is cleared to return. For now, Cooks' next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Hodge reverted to the 49ers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With the Niners still dealing with several injuries at wide receiver, Hodge appeared in his fourth game this season and played 12 offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Raiders. He caught his lone target for 17 yards and has two grabs for 35 yards this season.

items.headline: James returned five kickoffs for 101 yards during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: James set the tone right out of halftime with a 49-yard kickoff return, although the yards gained were mitigated by a holding penalty by the Niners. All eight of his snaps came on special teams, and it looks like the second-year pro is out of the mix for backfield touches behind RB1 Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, the latter of whom found the end zone for the second time in his last three outings. The 49ers will travel to Mexico City for Week 11 to face the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.headline: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
items.summary: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

items.headline: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

items.headline: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

items.headline: The 49ers placed Kirk (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Kirk made his season debut in San Francisco's last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, going without a target on a 30 percent snap share. After a Week 8 bye, he showed up on the initial Week 9 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a knee injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to be to the wide receiver's meniscus Friday, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com. Shanahan also relayed that Robinson may need surgery, but at the very least he'll miss the team's next four contests.

items.headline: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

items.headline: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
items.summary: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

items.headline: Foster reverted to the Seahawks' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Foster logged his first career regular-season offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Cardinals but didn't touch the ball on five plays he was in for. He's appeared in three contests for Seattle this season, seeing 10 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Holani is week-to-week after suffering an MCL sprain in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday.
items.summary: Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

items.headline: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

items.headline: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
items.summary: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.
items.summary: Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

items.headline: The Seahawks released Jones on Friday, Howard Balzer of USA Today reports. He was then signed back to the team's practice squad, per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com.
items.summary: Jones has been dealing with a hamstring injury and was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday after missing Monday's loss to the Bears. He didn't appear on the practice report Friday because Seattle decided to let the veteran running back go. However, Jones agreed to re-sign as part of the club's practice squad later in the day, so he'll now serve as depth in case injuries strike the Seahawks' running-back room again.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed Martinez to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: With Sam Darnold (quad) week-to-week, Martinez gives Seattle another body at quarterback. He logged one regular-season snap with San Francisco last season.

items.headline: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

items.headline: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
items.summary: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

items.headline: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

items.headline: The Buccaneers appear to be preparing for the possibility of Mayfield (foot) being sidelined for Sunday's game against the Lions, after the team signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad and signed Easton Stick to the 53-man roster Monday, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: Mayfield sustained a foot sprain when he was sacked during the fourth quarter of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears, and he doesn't appear to have made a full recovery from the injury coming out of a Week 10 bye. After Mayfield was reportedly in and out of a walking boot throughout the bye week, the Buccaneers opted to make a couple of transactions Monday to stabilize their quarterback room. The Buccaneers will likely wait and see how Mayfield progresses during the week before making a call on his status for Sunday, but if he's unable to take any reps with the first-team offense during practice, Jalon Daniels would be in line to start in Detroit. Daniels previously went 1-2 as a starter while Mayfield was sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated right thumb.

items.headline: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

items.headline: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

items.headline: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
items.summary: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

items.headline: Rush is in line to sign with the Buccaneers' practice squad, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.summary: Rush will give Tampa Bay added QB depth with starter Baker Mayfield dealing with an injury to his foot and ankle area that he sustained in Week 9. Jalon Daniels currently is Mayfield's top backup ahead of Week 11 action, while Easton Stick is on the team's practice squad.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

items.headline: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
items.summary: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

items.headline: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

items.headline: Restrepo reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Restrepo caught three passes for 31 yards in Sunday's loss to the Jaguars. The wide receiver played 19 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. Restrepo will likely have his final practice squad elevation of the 2026 regular season utilized in the Titans' Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys.

items.headline: Robinson is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jaguars due to an ankle injury.
items.summary: The Titans were already without Carnell Tate (shoulder) Sunday, and the team's receiver depth took another hit when Robinson appeared to sustain the injury late in the third quarter. If Robinson is unable to check back into the contest, he'll finish the game with three catches for 10 yards on four targets.

items.headline: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.summary: Singleton remains a healthy scratch for Week 10. The fifth-round rookie has played in four contests, logging seven rush attempts for 12 yards. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are set to continue as the main rushers for the Titans' offense.

items.headline: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target.
items.summary: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Spears returned to play 16 offensive snaps. Tony Pollard (41 snaps) remains the clear-cut lead back on this cellar-dwelling Tennessee team. Spears has minimal fantasy appeal now that Pollard survived the trade deadline and will finish out the season with the Titans.

items.headline: The Titans signed Brownlee to the practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Brownlee spent about a week on the Giants' practice squad before being cut by the team Oct. 27. He last saw regular-season action in 2025 with the Chiefs, when he saw just one target without recording a catch across six games. Wide receivers Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) are both working through injuries, although the former is expected to return from a two-game absence to play in Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday.

items.headline: Bradley reverted to the Commanders' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Bradley appeared in his first career regular-season game in Sunday's loss to the Rams, recording one catch for 12 yards across 17 offensive snaps. He could get some more run in the coming weeks if Dyami Brown (calf) remains sidelined for Washington.

items.headline: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants.
items.summary: Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

items.headline: head coach Dan Quinn said Monday that while the 21-day practice window for Croskey-Merritt (groin) hasn't been opened yet, he notes that the running back is "trending in the right direction," Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Croskey-Merritt landed on IR back on Oct. 19, but now that the running back has missed the required four games his stint on the list entailed, he's eligible to return to practice once he's ready to do so. Quinn's comment Monday suggests that's not an imminent outcome, though Croskey-Merritt's Week 11 outlook could brighten by the time the Commanders' first injury report ahead of next Monday's game against the Bengals is posted. In Washington's latest game -- a Nov. 12 24-21 win over the Giants -- Rachaad White (11 carries, one catch) and Austin Ekeler (nine carries, four catches) handled the bulk of the team's backfield load in Week 10.

items.headline: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

items.headline: The Commanders claimed Henry off waivers from the Seahawks on Tuesday.
items.summary: After being cut by Seattle on Monday, Henry quickly caught on with the Commanders. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA had previously joined the Commanders for training camp and the preseason, only to be waived prior to Week 1. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve for at least two more games and Jeremy McNichols (foot) likely to miss the remainder of the season, Henry will provide the Commanders with another option in the backfield behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. Henry didn't end up making his NFL debut during his time on the Seahawks roster.

items.headline: Jefferson caught five of seven targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: With Terry McLaurin (knee) and Treylon Burks (foot) out for the Commanders, Jefferson played 36 of 62 offensive snaps and ran 25 routes on Jayden Daniels' 42 dropbacks. The veteran wideout was signed to the active roster from the practice squad two weeks ago and led the team in receiving against Los Angeles. If Burks needs to miss more time, Jefferson could again have a role in three-wide sets Thursday night against the Giants.

items.headline: Kaliakmanis (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Giants but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Kaliakmanis is inactive once again. However, if Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection, Kaliakmanis will be available to play.

items.headline: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
items.summary: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

items.headline: White rushed 11 times for 47 yards and brought in one of two targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: White led the Commanders' ground attack once again, posting a team high in rushing yards and tying for the team lead in rush attempts with Jayden Daniels. The veteran back wasn't as involved as usual as a receiver, however, capping the overall quality of his fantasy performance. White also could see Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) make his return for a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23, a development that would likely relegate the former to a complementary role he'd presumably share with Austin Ekeler.

items.headline: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn ruled out Yankoff (knee) for Thursday night's games against the Giants, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports.
items.summary: Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not presumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

items.headline: The Commanders placed Brown (calf) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

items.headline: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.
